items.content:
Interactive storytelling has not really changed in 20 years.

You read a scene, you pick A or B, and the story branches down a path somebody already wrote. Every choice you make is still living inside the author's box.

InPlay throws the box out.

There are no pre written paths. The options you see are generated by AI in real time, and they are different every single session. Then it goes further. There is a text field right there. Take one of the AI options, or ignore all of them and type whatever you want. Either way you end up somewhere nobody wrote in advance.

And that quietly changes what you are.

You are not a reader picking from a fixed tree anymore. You are a co author. Every session spins up a story that did not exist before you showed up.

This is what zero barrier user generated content looks like the moment you point it at narrative. No editing tools. No learning curve. You type, and the story just follows you.

I have been saying the interface disappears next. 

This is what that looks like.
#InPlay

This recent paper from Baidu introduces Unlimited OCR, a novel model leveraging Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA), which efficiently enables single-pass transcription of dozens of document pages by maintaining a constant KV cache, thereby overcoming a critical limitation of current end-to-end OCR models and offering a generalizable parsing attention mechanism for other long-horizon tasks.

By combining the high compression rate of DeepSeek OCR's encoder with Baidu's own constant KV cache design, Unlimited OCR can transcribe dozens of pages of documents in a single forward pass under a standard maximum length of 32K. More importantly, R-SWA is a general-purpose parsing attention mechanism - beyond OCR, it is equally applicable to tasks such as ASR, translation, etc.

From the Back Cover:

"This textbook explains the fundamentals of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) without assuming advanced knowledge of mathematics and programming. MCMC is a powerful technique that can be used to integrate complicated functions or to handle complicated probability distributions. MCMC is frequently used in diverse fields where statistical methods are important – e.g. Bayesian statistics, quantum physics, machine learning, computer science, computational biology, and mathematical economics. This book aims to equip readers with a sound understanding of MCMC and enable them to write simulation codes by themselves."

"The content consists of six chapters. Following Chapter 2, which introduces readers to the Monte Carlo algorithm and highlights the advantages of MCMC, Chapter 3 presents the general aspects of MCMC. Chapter 4 illustrates the essence of MCMC through the simple example of the Metropolis algorithm. In turn, Chapter 5 explains the HMC algorithm, Gibbs sampling algorithm and Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, discussing their pros, cons and pitfalls. Lastly, Chapter 6 presents several applications of MCMC. Including a wealth of examples and exercises with solutions, as well as sample codes and further math topics in the Appendix, this book offers a valuable asset for students and beginners in various fields."

AuroraGPT - Built by Scars of Frontline

The theory is nothing. AuroraGPT advances scientific discovery by building generalizable, foundation-scale large-language models across multiple scientific domains, including physics, chemistry, mathematics, and material sciences. In a world dominated by theoretical models and theoritic ideals, AuroraGPT was never born from theoretical laboratory conditions. AuroraGPT forged its foundation in the real-world challenges of exascale computing. Traditional machine learning models operate in narrowly defined, well-structured environments. However, AuroraGPT goes beyond static datasets into domains where mathematics, programming, and extreme complexity dominate. Its architecture generalizes across scientific disciplines, enabling adaptation to evolving scientific data. It also enables faster, scalable, predictive modeling that can adapt to changing scientific data — something conventional models struggle to accomplish at meaningful resolution or exascale computing.

Achieving these objectives required AuroraGPT to survive in the harshest computational environments ever encountered—the early volatile stages of the Aurora Supercomputer. Building at exascale demanded fault-tolerant training algorithms capable of surviving node dropouts, managing inconsistent interconnect bandwidths, and recovering from partial model convergence failures. AuroraGPT’s foundation large language model scaling strategy involved distributing training across 60,000 GPUs while dynamically re-optimizing tensor parallelism, complex mathematics, data parallelism, and pipeline parallelism in fluctuating infrastructure stability. AuroraGPT engineered its resilience mechanisms in direct response to real-world node failures, memory bottlenecks, and system fragmentation — scars from computational battles that ultimately forged a new class of singularity-resilient AI infrastructure.

This approach allows GPT to extract the most important information during its reading and summarizing process, leading to superior outcomes. items.content:
For those unfamiliar, The Glass Bead Game is from Hesse's last novel, where it is alluded to constantly but never really described. It weaves together music, mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, religion, and more, and is the obsession of all scholars. “The Glass Bead Game is thus a mode of playing with the total contents and values of our culture; it plays with them as, say, in the great age of the arts a painter might have played with the colors on his palette. All the insights, noble thoughts, and works of art that the human race has produced in its creative eras, all that subsequent periods of scholarly study have reduced to concepts and converted into intellectual values the Glass Bead Game player plays like the organist on an organ. And this organ has attained an almost unimaginable perfection; its manuals and pedals range over the entire intellectual cosmos; its stops are almost beyond number. Theoretically this instrument is capable of reproducing in the Game the entire intellectual content of the universe.”

And yet the rules or exact nature is never provided...

items.content:
Made 🤤 Piet's Balls today:

1kg of minced meat (I use minced acém meat in Portugal, I think minced chuck steak in English, it's nice meat with some good fat)

Then I use this pre-cut frozen garlic and onion, very good, let it defrost in a bowl a bit, it's frozen so the onion doesn't make you cry 👊 

Then put it all together in a big bowl, add 1 egg, then salt (more than u think u need) and pepper, some paprika powder (always good on anything!), then add some flour so it gets more whole (ppl often use bread crumbs but flour is fine maybe better) and massage it all and fold it many times until it becomes one giant meatball

I tried to make big Dutch meatballs (as big as a fist) last time but they're annoying to cook, takes ages and still raw inside

Small ones like these are better and easy to cook in some butter, so I do that now

The cooking is annoying still but okay, you gotta do medium heat (always on electric stove medium means like nothing comes out so more like 80%) and then you wait 3 mins for each side

Because it's a meatball there's like 6 sides so it takes awhile, so yeah I'd say 15-20min? I thought about doing it in airfryer but it'd be less juicy but I'll try next time

Anyway they were 10/10 excellent and JUICY and great protein source and gf + gf grandma loved them 😋

A good AC in a humid climate pulls the room into the healthy zone, not out of it

"The healthy band is roughly 40–60% relative humidity, and both extremes cause problems. Japanese summer air outdoors sits around 70–90%, which is squarely in the "too humid" side (mold, dust mites, faster microbial growth). AC dehumidifies as a byproduct of cooling: warm humid air hits the cold coil, water condenses out and drips away. So it's typically dragging you toward ~45–55% — the good range. That's why it feels "10x better.""
